120450101.text: Aisa Bathhouse... Well, based on the letter, this should be the place.

120450102.text: It looks familiar... Hm, we've walked past here several times before, right? Just never gone inside.

120450103.text: Are you here to visit the Aisa Bathhouse?

120450105.text: Oh, sorry... Forgive me, I didn't mean to intrude. We've been struggling to attract customers recently, so I got a little over-excited when I heard you discussing my bathhouse...

120450106.text: "Your" bathhouse? So you run the place, huh? And business isn't going so great, you say?

120450107.text: Oops... please, forget I said that, it just slipped out. Now, do you have an appointment?

120450108.text: Uhh... we have a VIP pass. Can we use it now?

120450109.text: What? ...Ugh, I've told them before, a promotional gimmick isn't gonna magically fix our business. Who issued this thing... Wait, is that Miss Yumemizuki's signature?

120450110.text: I'm so sorry, I had no idea you were invited here by Miss Yumemizuki... Please, feel free to redeem your VIP pass now if you'd like. Just give your names at reception.

120450111.text: Sounds like she has a lot of clout... But aren't you supposed to be the boss?

120450112.text: I am, yes, but Miss Yumemizuki is a major shareholder. The business never would've gotten off the ground without her investment...

120450114.text: It's no cause for alarm though — she's a very responsible person. In addition to being a shareholder, she's also personally involved in our day-to-day business.

120450115.text: She only returned to Inazuma recently — otherwise, I'm sure you'd have heard of her by now. She's a highly renowned clinical psychologist.

120450201.text: An indoor hot spring? Paimon's gotta give that a try!

120450202.text: Hello! I'll be right with you— Aah!

120450204.text: *grimace* ...Sorry! I'm so clumsy sometimes... But don't worry about me! Putting customers in a bad mood is the last thing I want.

120450205.text: I promise I'll provide an excellent service! P—Please don't leave...

120450207.text: How many times do I have to tell you? You breaking a few plates isn't the reason we've been losing business. Stop apologizing for yourself all the time — all it does is make you look like an easy target.

120450208.text: It's all good, we're not out to target anyone... You didn't hurt yourself, did you?

120450209.text: ...Nope, don't worry! As long as it didn't ruin your experience, that's all that matters! Now, um... looks like you'll be my first customers today, so, so... according to our standards of service, I need to, um, umm...

120450213.text: Shion, let me see to these two. They're my guests.

120450214.text: Aha, there she is! Baku lady is back!

120450215.text: So Mizuki invited you here? As VIPs? ...Does this mean you're gonna save the Bathhouse!?

120450217.text: She means, you must be very wealthy. Not everyone can afford our VIP service, after all.

120450218.text: But a couple of customers with cash to splash doesn't solve anything in the long run. You should focus on what to do about our new competitor.

120450219.text: Aw, Murasaki, was that you showing some concern for our business? I'm touched.

120450221.text: Since you're so eager to find solutions, you can work on our most pressing task — bringing our accounts up to date. With your smarts, I'm sure you'll fly through it.

120450222.text: ...Subtext being, you can't give it to Shion, because she's a moron and she'd screw it up?

120450223.text: Shion, I'll take things from here. What I'd like you to do is head to the kitchen and prepare some of your very best snacks for our VIPs.

120450225.text: Sorry to keep you waiting. I have to keep our staff calm to ensure you have the best experience.

120450226.text: The panicky little girl is Hyakujitsuhaku Shion, and the lazy lady is Shiba Murasaki. They're both baku, just like me.

120450227.text: Wait... so the older-looking one is actually younger? And the younger-looking one is older?

120450228.text: That's right. How we choose to appear is just a matter of personal preference. It's more reflective of our personality than our age.

120450231.text: Anyway, enough about them — back to you two. Per the terms of the VIP pass, you're entitled to free use of all our services: so the spa, the fine dining, and psychological consultancy.

120450232.text: I would recommend starting with the psychological consultancy. Between me and you, one of the steps involves getting your bad dreams eaten.

120450233.text: #Since I ate one of {NICKNAME}'s good dreams by accident, this seemed like the best way to make amends.

120450234.text: Ooh, we get to have our bad dreams eaten by a yumekui-baku? That sounds fun!

120450235.text: But is this a wise decision, given the current state of the business?

120450236.text: That's a good point. You've been having some difficulties recently, right? It wouldn't feel right to get all this free service while you're struggling... Is there anything we can do to help out?

120450237.text: ...I take it you overheard Mr. Aikawa complaining about our current situation?

120450239.text: I am sorry to cause you concern. Mr. Aikawa is a smart businessman, but he tends to worry too much about short-term profits and lose sight of the big picture.

120450240.text: Our financial situation is nowhere near as dire as you're imagining. And in any case, passing our business woes onto our customers is hardly the solution.

120450241.text: Please enjoy the services we have to offer. Once you've experienced our hospitality for yourselves, I'm quite sure your confidence in our future prospects will be restored.

120450242.text: Can't argue with that! Let's get started!

120450243.text: Of course. The only thing is, psychological consultancy is a one-on-one service that takes quite a long time. But I can't just make one of you wait around while the other one is in therapy.

120450244.text: #So... Perhaps I can treat {NICKNAME} while Shion treats Paimon? Would that work?

120450245.text: Fine by Paimon! But uh... is she up for it?

120450246.text: She'll be fine. I noticed how gentle and encouraging you were towards her earlier. You're the perfect client for her.

120450248.text: Secondly, Shion's therapeutic approach is a little different from mine... it often involves food. So she might be a better fit for you.

120450249.text: Food therapy? Oh, that sounds perfect!

120450251.text: Was all that just so you could be paired with me?

120450252.text: Don't get me wrong, Paimon is genuinely better suited to Shion. But in all honesty — yes, I had my own reasons for wanting to treat you myself.

120450253.text: Your psychology is so unique. I just had to investigate further to satisfy my own curiosity.

120450701.text: Before we begin, please take a seat on this chair.

120450801.text: There's a theory which suggests that we bury our most powerful emotions deep within our dreams. That's the territory I would like to explore.

120450802.text: Before I start, I'm going to ask you a few questions. I want you to nod your head for yes and shake your head for no. Alright?

120450803.text: Very good. Now, I am going to plant a few thoughts in your subconscious, but it's nothing to get nervous about. Just a way to improve your sleep quality so the treatment will be more effective.

120450804.text: What's the problem? Are you expecting me to bribe you with candy like a little child?

120450805.text: Are we going to keep testing my patience?

120450806.text: Are you... trying to relax your neck muscles? Remind me to teach you the proper technique some time.

120450807.text: #...{NICKNAME}? Hellooo? It's not time to fall asleep just yet.

120450808.text: This is an incense from Sumeru that soothes the mind. The fragrance is said to be the "scent of dreams."

120450809.text: Now, close your eyes, take a deep breath, and concentrate on the scent.

120450810.text: The next step requires some visual preparation. So don't open your eyes until I say so.

120450812.text: *sigh* I need to have a stern talk with Murasaki. How hard is it to just put things back where they came from...

120450813.text: Hmm... This needs another dab here.

120450815.text: What is Mizuki looking for? Surely it can't hurt to take a quick peek?

120450816.text: I said no peeping... I'm still not ready yet.

120450817.text: Hey, don't run off now, darlings.

120450819.text: For goodness' sake, your butt's showing...

120450821.text: "Darlings"? Now I'm curious... Maybe just a sneaky little peek?

120450822.text: *sigh* Let me do that for you.

120450823.text: I can see that you don't like being kept waiting. Go on, open your eyes. Everything's ready.

120450824.text: Ready. You can open your eyes now.

120450825.text: You kept your eyes closed the entire time! If only every patient was as compliant as you, it'd make our lives much easier... Here, you deserve a treat.

120450826.text: Take a good look at this painting — there are some very special little darlings hidden within it, and I'd like you to find them.

120450827.text: Do you see her? Isn't she just adorable?

120450828.text: Now, you just need to find the others.

120450829.text: Oh, are your eyes feeling sore? If so, please feel free to take a break.

120450830.text: Careful. When you look a psychologist directly in the eyes, they can see every little thing you are thinking.

120450831.text: She's a baku as well. Whenever someone starts dozing off, she's there waiting for their dream to begin.

120450832.text: Your journey into dreamland began as you were looking for them. Feeling sleepy?

120450833.text: Now, I want you to take my hand.

120450834.text: What's the matter? Feeling shy? Relax, this is just a part of the psychotherapeutic technique.

120450835.text: Very good. Now, close your eyes again for me.

120450836.text: I want you to completely relax, and focus your attention on the feeling of my palm touching yours. Notice how all other sensations in your body are slowly fading away...

120450837.text: Now, imagine you're holding not my hand, but your favorite things in all of the world.

120450838.text: You run your hand through the sakura blossoms gently falling through the air, then through a squirrel's fur... Then you grab a fistful of sand on the beach...

120450839.text: You are once again in the wilderness, running with the wind at your back. But slowly, your palm loses sensation. You lose your way and find yourself surrounded by darkness.

120450840.text: You can't see anything. But you hear someone calling you... and now, a light is shining from the same direction as their voice...

120450903.text: Longing, caused by separation... It tastes so bitter. Please, don't stop moving.

120450904.text: Despair, caused by failure... Icy-cold on the lips. Please, keep going.

120450905.text: Regret, caused by missed opportunity... A sharp aftertaste. Please, don't look back.

120450906.text: Go to where the sakura petals fall, go to where the squirrels play, go to where you can hear the sound of the waves...

120451001.text: Holding my hand tight, those lost sensations come back to you...

120451002.text: The feeling of running your hand through falling sakura blossoms, or through a squirrel's fur, or of grabbing a fistful of sand on the beach...

120451003.text: And as you return from the wilderness, you gradually recover your other senses as well.

120451004.text: We've reached the end of today's session. Don't get up yet, though — you were just in a very deep sleep, so you're probably still feeling a little groggy. I've switched to a different incense that'll help get rid of your drowsiness.

120451007.text: How are you feeling after your session, Paimon?

120451008.text: Hmm... Kinda... fresher and more relaxed? It feels... cozy, somehow.

120451009.text: Good — that's exactly how you should feel after having a nightmare eaten. It sounds like the session was quite effective.

120451010.text: Oh, for sure! Paimon especially liked how she used the sense of taste to help guide the process.

120451011.text: But Paimon was asleep for most of it, so she's not really sure how it all works. Do the yumekui-baku just, like... sneak into your brain and gulp down your bad dreams in one go?

120451012.text: It's quite a bit more complicated than that. It deals with people's most visceral emotions, which have to be handled with the utmost care and attention...

120451014.text: ...Sorry, that probably made no sense at all. Anyway, don't worry about the details. For your purposes, Paimon, just think of it as Shion gulped your dreams away.

120451018.text: Really? Hmm... I still think there's more work to be done...

120451020.text: You have quite a reputation for resilience and positivity. So, I expected to find very few negative emotions in you at all.

120451021.text: But when I was deep in your subconscious earlier, the sheer weight of the emotions hidden there was overwhelming...

120450301.text: Hmm... Most impressive, I must say...

120450303.text: Ah, there you are... I heard a rumor that you were about to be kidnapped. Naturally, I had to come and see it for myself.

120450304.text: ...She's joking, right? Paimon can never quite tell with her.

120450307.text: She never mentioned? Interesting... We've known each other since before I became the Guuji. I've told her all about you... but it sounds like she's forgotten all about me.

120450308.text: #You'll have to forgive me. I just didn't want to scare {NICKNAME} off... and "Hi, I'm Miko's friend" seemed like a sure-fire way to do that.

120450312.text: Ah, I've missed your way with words.

120450313.text: So, Lady Guuji. To what do we owe the honor?

120450314.text: Why, I simply came to see the business that my dear friend has invested in... Oh, and also to urge you to sell your shares before their value plummets to nothing.

120450315.text: You could always invest in the Yae Publishing House, you know... Business is always booming. You only need to ask.

120450316.text: Sounds serious... But what's wrong? Are the shares really gonna plummet to nothing?

120450317.text: Hasn't she told you? ...Tsk, of course. She's your therapist — she has the perfect excuse to never open up.

120450318.text: The Aisa Bathhouse used to be very popular — although not because of the hot springs, despite the name. Their main selling point has always been the psychotherapy services offered by the baku.

120450319.text: But recently, a competitor cropped up... His name is Emura Ichigensai. He operates right here on Narukami Island, and his methods are said to be quite revolutionary.

120450320.text: Since he provides a similar service to the bathhouse and boasts even better results, he was able to poach their entire clientele in just a matter of days.

120450321.text: *sigh* It's such a pity to see how empty this place is now.

120450322.text: Miko, my job is to relieve my clients of their burdens — not to share mine with them.

120450323.text: Of course you'd say that — you're a professional. But no amount of professionalism is going to fix this situation, is it?

120450324.text: I heard people have been lining up since the early morning for Emura Ichigensai's clinic today — he's seeing patients just west of Inazuma City. And how many patients have you seen today?

120450325.text: ...Surely you know I'm not going to quit?

120450327.text: ...So that's it? You're just gonna leave?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the address Miko mentioned

120450401.text: This should be the place... That guy looks official. Let's go ask him.

120450402.text: Hi there! We're looking for Emura Ichigensai, are we in the right—

120450403.text: Pay first, take a ticket, then wait your turn.

120450405.text: Ninety-seven... What number are you up to so far?

120450406.text: Fifty-three. Be patient. I'll call your number when it's your turn.

120450407.text: Geez, what a charmer... Looks like we're in for a long wait, huh?

120450409.text: Sounds kinda therapeutic in its own way... But we don't really have a good excuse to resort to violence here. And we definitely don't wanna scare off our target.

120450410.text: Why don't we pass the time by talking to some of his other patients? It looks like there's a few of them standing over there.

120450412.text: Hey, good idea! Hmm, it looks like there's a few of them over there. Let's go see what we can find out.

subQuests.subQuestName: Ask around for information on Emura Ichigensai

120450504.text: ...Ah, so you're here for counselling too.

120450505.text: Yep! Fellow clients of Emura Ichigensai here. Although, this'll be our first time using his service, so—

120450506.text: "Service"? How crass. We're talking about spiritual guidance here, not some business transaction!

120450507.text: In fairness to them, they haven't experienced it yet. Ignorance among the uninitiated is only to be expected.

120450508.text: Okay... Well anyway, Aisa Bathhouse calls it a service...

120450509.text: Ah, more defectors from the bathhouse, huh? "Service" might have a veneer of professionalism, but all it really means is inadequate treatment that costs a fortune.

120450511.text: I'll tell you why. After just a few sessions with Emura Ichigensai, you'll completely forget about all your troubles. From then on, it's happy thoughts only!

120450512.text: Today's supposed to be my last counselling session. He says that after we're done, nothing will ever trouble me again!

120450513.text: Meanwhile, Aisa Bathhouse boasts about their strange and mysterious methods, but it's a total scam. They only treat the symptoms, not the root cause, meaning you have to go back time after time — all so they can keep charging you, of course.

120450514.text: Exactly. Overpriced and ineffective. But counselling from Emura Ichigensai? I can't get enough! I know I'm done after today, but I'd take any excuse to keep coming back!

120450515.text: Me too... Probably see you tomorrow, then.

120450516.text: Whatever the truth of the matter is, Paimon is starting to seriously dislike these guys!

120450519.text: Fine... Yeah, so we're mostly here to see what all the fuss is about. You guys seem to be experts by now — is there anything we need to do to prepare for our session?

120450520.text: No, you don't need to do anything.

120450521.text: Just show up, take a seat, and he takes care of the rest. I remember he lit some incense... it smelled wonderful, and instantly relaxed me...

120450522.text: I already know of the troubles that bring you to me.

120450523.text: I don't know why I lose my temper so easily... I'm pretty messed up, right?

120450524.text: Yes, in the sense that all negative emotions are defects of the mind. But I can remove these defective feelings, leaving your mind healthy, whole, and free of distressing thoughts.

120450526.text: I don't actually remember the guidance... But anyway, it clearly worked. I guess whatever he said disappeared from my mind and took my problems along with it.

120451501.text: Pay first, take a ticket, then wait your turn.

120451403.text: Yawn... that was a long wait. Paimon's gonna need a nap after this, too.

120451404.text: No problem. It's my turn to keep watch anyway.

120451405.text: Alright! Now, time for us to go meet Mr. Emura Ichigensai!

120450601.text: Oh, hello! We're number 97. It should be our turn now, right?

120450602.text: Uhhh... Yeah, sorry, the clinic's closed for the day.

120450604.text: Because Emura Ichigensai doesn't have limitless energy, that's why. He's gone home to rest. You'll have to try again tomorrow.

120450605.text: But we've been waiting sooooo long!

120450606.text: Not as long as some people. Try getting here earlier next time.

120450607.text: Do you know where he lives, by any chance?

120450608.text: Hah, save yourself the trouble. Spiritual masters like Emura Ichigensai cultivate their powers with peace and solitude. Someone like you ain't gonna find him.

120450609.text: Drat. We shoulda barged in after all...

120450610.text: Let's report back to Mizuki for now.

120450611.text: Yeah, nothing else we can do for today.

120451101.text: You tell Mizuki everything you saw and heard today.

120451102.text: So he gives spiritual guidance... And it takes all your troubles away and leaves only happy thoughts?

120451103.text: Yup. At least, that's what his clients say.

120451104.text: How is that possible? Not even Mizuki could do that, and she's an incredible psychologist.

120451105.text: Is that right? Paimon was gonna say, it all sounds too good to be true...

120451106.text: It certainly is. Humans are... how to put this... they're a moody race — always upset about something. Show me a human without a care in the world, and I'll show you what "messed up" really looks like.

120451107.text: You think? 'Cause honestly, they sounded pretty convincing. And they said they only left the Aisa Bathhouse because they found it didn't deal with the root cause of their issues.

120451108.text: But the idea he is spreading is categorically wrong...

120451109.text: That settles it, then. Emura Ichigensai is a quack, making false claims to steal all our customers.

120451110.text: Is that why he's doing this? To steal... steal our customers? Or is there more to it?

120451111.text: ...It's unfortunate that you didn't get to meet him in person. I need some idea of the kind of person he is. Otherwise, I have no hope of figuring out his motivations and goals.

120451112.text: Yeah, it's too bad... Although if it's any help, we did hear a bit about his backstory from someone else. Apparently, he used to have a really rotten temper, but then one day he suddenly reached enlightenment and became a spiritual master, or something...

120451113.text: Emura Ichigensai... rotten temper... Now wait just a minute...

120451114.text: Filing patient records is normally the most tedious job in the world. But once in a while, something mildly amusing grabs my attention. Take a look at this.

120451118.text: What is it? What about him?

120451119.text: Where to start? ...Imagine a big ball of negative emotion took on human form and started walking around. That's pretty much Emura Chuuya.

120451120.text: His patient record mentions that he loved nothing more than a heated argument. No matter how trivial it was, he could never agree to disagree — he always had to be right. The happiest part of his day would be winning an argument and proving the other person wrong.

120451121.text: If he lost, he'd sulk, and if anyone called him out, he'd throw a huge tantrum. Before long, he'd turned everyone against him.

120451124.text: Anyway, since no one would talk to him in real life anymore, he turned to the readers' letters column of a magazine by the Yae Publishing House, where he would attack writers and trade insults with other contributors.

120451125.text: Naturally, this ruined the column for everyone, and the editor soon started rejecting his letters.

120451126.text: Next thing you know, he's written a complaint letter to the Tenryou Commission, demanding that Inazuma pass a law to make it illegal for the Yae Publishing House to reject letters from readers...

120451127.text: Gee whizz... Where would you even start with a client like that?

120451128.text: In my case — by giving them a wide berth. Mizuki dealt with this guy.

120451129.text: I'm pretty sure he only came here to try and start something. But Mizuki managed to get him into a session, and after some treatment, his mood improved by a lot.

120451131.text: Murasaki makes him sound like a rabid animal... He wasn't THAT out of control. Sure, his personality was very abrasive, but it wasn't hard to see why.

120451132.text: Once I understood his situation, I was able to diagnose him very quickly...

120451133.text: You have very high expectations for yourself, but you've faced a lot of rejection in the past and haven't achieved much in your life.

120451134.text: You've never had any real close friends, so you don't know what healthy connections with other people look like. This puts you and your ego in the center of your world.

120451135.text: In short, you long to feel a sense of accomplishment and to receive attention from other people. But both of these are lacking in your life.

120451136.text: You have no idea how to properly deal with these emotions. So you've been taking it out on other people, partly to seek attention, and partly because you get a shallow sense of accomplishment whenever you win a war of words with another person.

120451137.text: Tsk... You promise the world with your adverts, and that's seriously the best you can come up with? I'm not even going to bother explaining all the reasons you're wrong...

120451138.text: I mean, you completely misunderstood why I even sent that complaint letter. The Yae Publishing House practically has a monopoly on Inazuma's publishing industry. How can they ignore what their readers have to say?

120451139.text: In the magazine column you wrote to, your strongly worded letter appeared alongside dozens of others which praised the writer for their work. You can't talk about what their readers have to say without including them, too.

120451140.text: No one with half a brain would praise a festering pile of garbage like that. Those are not opinions worth listening to.

120451141.text: So, when I touched on the idea of you having an egocentric worldview — this is the kind of thing I was talking about.

120451143.text: Wow... How the heck did you get him to stay for treatment after dropping all of that on him?

120451144.text: Simple. The more he realized the truth of my diagnosis, the more he compulsively searched for evidence to refute it with.

120451145.text: He'd lost the ability to communicate like a normal human being. So, I kept him here by using his preferred mode of interaction: argumentation.

120451146.text: The Tenryou Commission had ignored his complaint letter, so he had no outlets left for his emotional outbursts.

120451147.text: Eventually, with the help of some incendiary words, I got him to agree to try some basic therapy. Finally, I was able to tweak his mood and stabilize his condition.

120451148.text: It's a shame, really — if I'd only been able to see him a few more times, I know I could've helped him work through his personality issues. But unfortunately...

120451150.text: For the last time, it was his fault for being a nutjob.

120451152.text: Well, one day, he comes in as usual for therapy, but Mizuki isn't here. So, Shion sees him instead.

120451153.text: I don't know what got into him that day, but he suddenly announced that he wished to be free of his troubles for good — and demanded that Shion make that happen.

120451154.text: Obviously, she didn't manage it, and then he pulled out a complaint letter to try and intimidate her. That was the last straw for me. I kicked him out and blacklisted him.

120451155.text: He hasn't shown his face here since.

120451157.text: Anyway, now everyone's had a look at his record — do we think there's any chance that this guy and Emura Ichigensai are the same person?

120451158.text: Because it sounds to me like after he didn't get what he wanted, he decided to have his revenge by lying to our customers and getting them to leave.

120451161.text: Bad dreams are formed from a buildup of negative emotions in the subconscious. You can't simply trick people into not having them anymore. If Murasaki was right, then surely they'd have seen his lies for what they are by now...

120451162.text: There's no point hemming and hawing! Let's report this guy to the Tenryou Commission for fraudulent business practices. If he can complain, so can we!

120451164.text: We'd like to book a therapy session... Can we start now?

120451165.text: Hello! Please come with me, I'll get you registered.

120451166.text: Wait, those are the two guys Paimon mentioned earlier! Just this morning, they were calling the bathhouse a scam and a rip-off. How are they back here already?

120451167.text: Oh really? Well, that proves it doesn't it? I was right. Now that they've realized they were lied to, they've come back.

120451168.text: So chin up, Mizuki. I bet you business will start picking up again from tomorrow morning.

120451169.text: Yeah! You yumekui-baku provide an unbeatable service, no scammer's gonna run you girls out of business!

120451170.text: Interesting... Well, good. Murasaki, go help Shion please.

120451171.text: Tch... Shoulda kept my mouth shut. I jinxed it, and now I have to work again.

120451172.text: Now we just need to report this guy as a fraud to the Tenryou Commission, like Murasaki suggested. Problem solved!

120451173.text: It looks like the Aisa Bathhouse will be back in business in no time. No idea if our investigation actually helped, though...

120451174.text: Of course it did. You were a huge help, and I owe you big time for it.

120451176.text: Now then. You only got part way through the VIP experience last time, didn't you? You still have to try the hot springs and snacks. Both are top tier.

120451177.text: Oh, true! How could Paimon forget about that? Especially the snacks!

120451178.text: After a dip in the hot springs and some delicious snacks, you and Paimon feel wonderfully relaxed.

120451179.text: Wow, Paimon feels incredible now. Nothing beats the complete service package!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to where you first met Mizuki

120451203.text: What? Why's Mizuki crying? Unless... Oh, maybe we got pulled into one of her bizarre dreams again?

120451204.text: #{NICKNAME}? Paimon? What are you doing here?

120451205.text: Well firstly, we were hoping to get our next appointment booked in...

120451206.text: ...Ah, I see. I was planning on making it back before you finished in the hot springs, but I ended up spending longer here than I intended.

120451207.text: Don't worry, this isn't a dream. I was just... feeling a little sad.

120451208.text: Aw, what's up? Indigestion getting you down again?

120451209.text: No, my digestion was fine this time. What you saw just now was the aftermath of the digestion process.

120451210.text: Like I said, bad dreams are basically bundles of all kinds of negative emotions. When I digest them, I feel them all for myself.

120451211.text: So when I'm processing these emotions, I tend to get quite... well, emotional.

120451212.text: Does that happen to all yumekui-baku?

120451213.text: Oh, don't worry about the others. To feel these emotions, you first have to understand them.

120451214.text: Most baku have a very poor understanding of humanity, so to them, a human bad dream just tastes like a slice of bland white bread. They can basically wolf it down and barely notice the flavor.

120451215.text: I'm the odd one out in that sense. When I was studying abroad, I made a serious effort to learn as much about human psychology as possible.

120451216.text: Now, I understand human emotions much better. I can empathize with them, and I can now discern many complex emotions when I turn my attention to digesting bad dreams.

120451217.text: But still, that's no reason for you to be concerned about me. I wouldn't be much of a psychologist if I didn't have the mental fortitude to handle this stuff.

120451218.text: Letting your emotions out is one of the most effective ways to process them. Now that I've done that, my mental state is back to normal.

120451219.text: Paimon thought maybe seeing those customers had upset you somehow.

120451220.text: It even makes Paimon mad! You work so hard for them, and then they turn around and accuse the bathhouse of being a money-making scam.

120451221.text: Yes, they were led astray by some swindler... but it's not like they took much persuading.

120451222.text: I can't blame them. The idea that you can forget all of your troubles and never have a bad dream again is a very alluring one. Who wouldn't want to believe that?

120451223.text: #{NICKNAME}, if I really could make you forget all of your troubles for good, would you want me to try?

120451225.text: As you imagine forgetting your pain and longing, the joy of reunion that you are looking forward to one day disappears along with it.

120451226.text: As you imagine letting go of your hopelessness, you also feel your fighting spirit slip through your fingers.

120451227.text: As you imagine being free from your painful regrets, the formative experiences of your journey lose their roots.

120451230.text: ...You really are different from other people.

120451231.text: Discovering what troubles people is easy for me — even in your case. But although I see your troubles clearly, I still don't completely understand you.

120451232.text: *sigh*... Thanks for checking in on me. As a psychologist, I know how to take care of myself, but you showing that you care is still appreciated.

120451233.text: Anyway, it's much too late to book another appointment now... You should head home, get some sleep, have a wonderful dream, and come see me again tomorrow.

120451236.text: Bye for now. If you still want to book another appointment tomorrow, make sure to come see me early.

120451237.text: #{NICKNAME}, if I really could make you forget all of your troubles for good, would you want me to try?

120451601.text: Uhhh... Yeah, sorry, the clinic's closed for the day.

120453001.text: Aren't you going to head inside? Believe me, Miss Yumemizuki will not disappoint!
